findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the reverse census direction is implemented: either add a third test that DISCOVERS every `python scripts/check_*.py` line in the lint-target body (via _lint_target_body) and asserts each is in _WIRED_GATES, or justify in the plan why the forward-only pair satisfies AC2's 'every make lint script appears in _WIRED_GATES'.
evidence: test_make_lint_hygiene_wiring.py:49-55 and :58-66 are both @parametrize over _WIRED_GATES and assert `script in body` / teeth -- forward direction only
No Makefile-discovery mechanism exists in the module (search for `check_` returns only docstring + the two literal _WIRED_GATES entries + a function name)
AC2 demands 'every make lint script appears in _WIRED_GATES' -- the reverse direction -- which no current or planned test implements
Plan: '_WIRED_GATES ... stays explicit by that module's design' -- an explicit list cannot enforce the reverse direction without a discovery assertion
findings.finding: The plan requires a bidirectional census (AC2: 'every make lint script appears in _WIRED_GATES and every _WIRED_GATES entry appears in make -n lint') but the census module it extends has only two parametrized tests that both assert the FORWARD direction (each _WIRED_GATES entry appears in the lint-target body). Neither test discovers scripts from the Makefile, so the REVERSE invariant -- a lint-target check_*.py script with no _WIRED_GATES entry -- is unenforced. Because the plan deletes 30 per-twin wiring tests and keeps an explicit (non-discovered) _WIRED_GATES list, a future lint script added without an owner-entry passes silently: the single census is weaker than the per-twin wiring tests it replaces.
findings.location: Approach ('the census module's two parametrized tests replace every deleted per-twin wiring test, so wiring has exactly one census'); AC line 2
scenarios: A new scripts/check_foo.py is wired into the lint target in a later change but the author forgets to add it to _WIRED_GATES -- the census is green, reproducing the exact silent-wiring regression this plan centralises away

The deleted per-twin 'make lint wires it' tests each anchored one named script; after deletion only the forward census remains, so coverage of 'this specific script is owned' shrinks to the subset someone remembered to list
findings.suggested_fix: Add a discovery-based test to the census module: parse the lint-target body with the existing _lint_target_body helper, extract every `scripts/check_*.py` invocation, and assert the extracted set equals set(_WIRED_GATES) (both directions). This makes _WIRED_GATES a checked mirror rather than a hand-maintained allowlist, closing the silent-add gap while preserving the 'no CI-only script sneaks in' intent.
